question: An engineer must implement a solution that prevents untrusted DHCP servers from compromising the network. The feature must be configured on a Cisco Nexus 7000 Series Switch and applied to VLAN 10. The legitimate DHCP servers are connected to interface Ethernet 2/4. Which configuration set must be used to meet these requirements?
options: n7k-1(config)# ip dhcp snooping vlan 10 n7k-1(config)# interface Ethernet2/4 n7k-1(config-if)# ip dhcp snooping verify vlan 10
n7k-1(config)# ip dhcp snooping verify n7k-1(config)# interface Ethernet2/4 n7k-1(config-if)# ip dhcp snooping verify vlan 10
n7k-1(config)# ip dhcp snooping vlan 10 n7k-1(config)# interface Ethernet2/4 n7k-1(config-if)# ip dhcp snooping trust
n7k-1(config)# ip dhcp snooping verify n7k-1(config)# vlan configuration 10 n7k-1(config-vlan)# ip dhcp snooping trust
theory: DHCP snooping filters traffic based on interface trust state: enabling ip dhcp snooping vlan 10 activates the feature for that VLAN, and marking the interface facing the legitimate DHCP server (Ethernet 2/4) as trusted with ip dhcp snooping trust exempts DHCP server-type replies (OFFER/ACK) arriving on that port from being dropped. All other, untrusted ports will have DHCP server responses (like those from a rogue DHCP server) filtered out automatically, since untrusted ports may only forward client-originated DHCP requests. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 - Nexus First-Hop Security, NX-OS DHCP Snooping)
